title: Microsoft 365 admin center: high-usage Copilot users list in Billing & usage
summary: Hold: the briefing turns the roadmap's feature title into a navigation route to a page that Microsoft Learn does not document. The existing licence-assignment and report-privacy controls are supported, and the roadmap dates and availability match the record.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Scope; rationale: risk and impact
claims.claim: The roadmap plans an administrator-facing high-usage users list in the Microsoft 365 admin center's Copilot Billing & usage area.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 admin center: Copilot - Billing & usage: High-usage users

claims.claim: The High-usage users view is reached under Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Billing & usage.
claims.quote: Searched: "High-usage users" "Copilot" "Billing & usage" admin center navigation. Opened Credits report and pay-as-you-go setup. They give routes for other billing controls, not this view; the roadmap title supplies no navigation steps.
claims.fix: Replace the first sentence with: "The roadmap item plans a High-usage users view in the Microsoft 365 admin center's Copilot Billing & usage area; its navigation path is not yet documented." Keep the roadmap attribution, but remove the asserted 'Copilot > Billing & usage' route.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The report privacy route is Settings > Org settings > Services > Reports > Conceal user, group, and site names in all reports in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: select Settings. ... Select Org Settings. ... On the Services tab, select Reports. ... In the Reports panel, uncheck the checkbox next to Conceal user, group, and site names in all reports.

claims.claim: PATCH /v1.0/admin/reportSettings updates tenant-level Microsoft 365 report settings.
claims.quote: Update tenant-level settings for Microsoft 365 reports. ... PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/admin/reportSettings

claims.claim: The report settings PATCH request uses the displayConcealedNames body property to control concealment.
claims.quote: displayConcealedNames | Boolean | If set to true, all reports conceal user information such as usernames, groups, and sites. If false, all reports show identifiable information.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Why it matters; Governance guidance

claims.claim: The usage-report concealment setting applies to the Credits report.
claims.quote: By default, user-specific information like usernames, display names, groups, and sites is hidden in usage reports. To learn how to display this information in usage reports, see Show user, group, or site details in usage reports.
